chunks: From Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdillah, from Zurarah ibn A'yan, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'How do I perform Tamattu'?' He said, 'You arrive at the time and respond with the call for Hajj. When you enter Mecca, you perform Tawaf around the House, pray two rak'ahs behind the Maqam, perform Sa'i between Safa and Marwah, shorten your prayer, and exit the state of Ihram from everything. And you are not permitted to leave Mecca until you perform Hajj.' Then there is a slight tension because these narrations are understood to apply to one who responds with Hajj and intends Umrah, for that is permissible in case of necessity and precaution; indeed, perhaps the intention is for Tamattu' to be superior, as indicated by what was narrated:

key_terms.أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far (Imam al-Baqir), the sixth Imam
key_terms.أَتَمَتَّعُ: To perform Tamattu' (a type of Hajj combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.أَحْلَلْتَ: To exit the state of Ihram
key_terms.الصَّفَا: Safa (one of the hills in Mecca)
key_terms.تُلَبِّي بِالْحَجِّ: To respond with the Talbiyah for Hajj
key_terms.سَعَيْتَ: To perform Sa'i (walking between Safa and Marwah)
key_terms.طُفْتَ بِالْبَيْتِ: To perform Tawaf (circumambulation) around the Kaaba
key_terms.قَصَّرْتَ: To shorten the four-rak'ah prayer to two

ai.seo_question: What are the steps to perform Umrah al-Tamattu' according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the ritual sequence for Umrah al-Tamattu', where the pilgrim performs Umrah rites—Tawaf, Sa'i, and Halq/Qasr—while remaining in a state of Ihram for Hajj. The text highlights a key Shia scholarly nuance: while the primary instruction assumes an intention of Hajj, the procedure is also applicable to those who explicitly intend Umrah, particularly under conditions of necessity or precaution (Taqiyyah), with some scholars considering Tamattu' superior due to the accumulation of rewards.
